ExampleScene is typed SceneProps&lt;{label:string}&gt;, which matches Scene&lt;Payload&gt;. Presentation requires steps and title, and Talk.tsx passes both plus the optional initialMode. Label and SceneLayer take NodeProps, whose props are all optional, and the template passes layoutId and children, which exist. The bootstrap tsconfig.app.json enables noUnusedLocals, noUnusedParameters and verbatimModuleSyntax; the templates use import type correctly and have no unused locals. entities.ts only exports entity, and &lt;slug&gt; appears only inside a string literal. The bootstrap&#39;s own starter presentation uses the same import shapes and field names against the same kit, and its registry entry imports &#39;./starter/Talk&#39; correctly. The inspect template (bootstrap/scripts/inspect-presentation.mjs) imports only node built-ins and playwright, and it is not in the tsconfig include of src, so it has no relative imports to resolve. Fixed: review_._all-reviewers (1) - src/presentation-kit/Stage.tsx:15 The scene key for a grouped step is inconsistent. Precondition: a group (`groupKey`) starts at index > 0, after a step with a different groupKey or none. Trace: at the group's first step, `previous` exists and `continuingGroup` is false, so `sceneKey` is `step.id`. At the group's second step, `continuingGroup` is true, so `sceneKey` becomes `step.groupKey`. The keyed `motion.div` changes from `step.id` to `groupKey`, so `AnimatePresence mode=\"wait\"` exits and remounts the scene. Failure: the grouped scene's shared-layout continuity breaks between its first and second steps. Local state is lost, `Appear` newcomers fade in again, and the exit and enter delays add visible lag. Only groups that start at index 0 behave correctly, and the test covers only that case.\n ✓ Fixed: review_._all-reviewers (1) - src/presentation-kit/Presentation.tsx:28 `setStage` is an inline ref callback that is recreated on every render, and it captures `nav.bindSwipe`, which changes whenever `next` or `prev` change (that is, on every index change). Trace: each render makes React call the old ref with null and the new ref with the element. The old swipe listeners are removed and new ones are bound. Failure: churn on every render, and a touch gesture whose `touchstart` and `touchend` straddle a re-render (for example, a resize or a `wideViewport` update) loses its `start` state, so the swipe is silently ignored. A single outline.map gives every step Scene: EvolvingScene and groupKey &#39;sample-evolving-scene&#39;. Stage.tsx turns that into sceneKey = `${groupKey}:${sceneIdentity(Scene)}` and uses it as the key of the motion.div canvas. Adjacent steps therefore keep the same key and the same Scene component, so the scene instance stays mounted and only the payload changes. A single shared groupKey is correct for this one continuously evolving scene. Entity identity is separate from groupKey. entities.ts defines entity(name) = &#39;how-to-make-a-presentation:&#39;+name. EvolvingScene.tsx passes entity(&#39;you&#39;), entity(&#39;skill&#39;), entity(&#39;step-N&#39;), entity(&#39;morph-N&#39;) and the other ids as layoutId to the kit nodes. Box, Arrow, SymbolChip, Label, Emphasis, Frame and SceneLayer forward layoutId to motion elements with layout, and Stage wraps them in a LayoutGroup. The ids are stable across steps, and entities that persist between steps keep the same id. For example, &#39;you&#39; appears at every step and &#39;skill&#39; from step 2 onward. Because the ids are stable, the kit&#39;s layout mechanism animates a persisting entity from its old state to its new one.","evidence":["steps.tsx: groupKey &#39;sample-evolving-scene&#39; on all nine mapped steps","Stage.tsx: sceneKey from groupKey plus sceneIdentity(step.Scene), used as the motion.div key","entities.ts: entity() helper","EvolvingScene.tsx: layoutId={entity(...)} on every node, including Arrow connectors","nodes/*.tsx: layout and layoutId forwarded to motion elements"],"citations":["src/presentations/how-to-make-a-presentation/steps/steps.tsx","src/presentations/how-to-make-a-presentation/steps/EvolvingScene.tsx","src/presentations/how-to-make-a-presentation/entities.ts","src/presentation-kit/Stage.tsx","src/presentation-kit/types.ts","src/presentation-kit/nodes/Box.tsx","src/presentation-kit/nodes/Arrow.tsx","src/presentation-kit/nodes/SymbolChip.tsx","src/presentation-kit/nodes/Label.tsx","src/presentation-kit/nodes/Emphasis.tsx","src/presentation-kit/nodes/Frame.tsx","src/presentation-kit/nodes/SceneLayer.tsx"],"family":"claude","model":"claude-sonnet-5-5","effort":"high","panel_index":0},{"id":"demo-stable-identity-and-grouping","verdict":"pass","rationale":"Grouping: `steps.tsx` builds all nine steps from one outline map with `Scene: EvolvingScene` and `groupKey: &#39;sample-evolving-scene&#39;`. `Stage` computes `sceneKey = groupKey:sceneIdentity(step.Scene)`, which is identical for every step. The single keyed `motion.div` inside `AnimatePresence` therefore stays mounted, and each step only passes a new `payload`/`index` to the same `SceneComponent`. The nine steps are generated by one map, so there is no per-step module to check. Identity: the presentation-owned `entity(name)` helper in `entities.ts` creates stable ids. `EvolvingScene` passes them as `layoutId` on every rendered node: you, prompt, skill, conversation, question, step-N, morph-N, ghost, verify, depth, kit-link, kit, modify, edited and reveal. The supplied files do none of that. SKILL.md only lists Playwright as a package. SIGINT and SIGTERM handlers also call stopPreview. In inspect, the spawn, readiness, browser launch, and every capture sit inside run()&#39;s try, and its finally calls stopPreview. That function sends SIGTERM, awaits &#39;exit&#39; (capped at 2s), then SIGKILL. Success, a failing check, a browser launch failure, and a later thrown error therefore all pass through the same awaited cleanup. The template copies are identical apart from the removed sample check, and the contract test enforces that. Judge C&#39;s reason does not decide the requirement. The SIGKILL without a second await is reached only when the server ignores SIGTERM for 2–3s. That is a hypothetical hang the candidate does not produce, not one of the named exit paths. On every named path the server is terminated and its exit awaited. All four copies spawn Vite&#39;s own binary with process.execPath, not through an npm or npx wrapper. The child they track is therefore the preview server itself. In verify, the preview is created in renderRoutes, and readiness, chromium.launch, and every route check all sit inside one try whose finally runs `await browser?.close(); await stopPreview()`. stopPreview sends SIGTERM to the process group and awaits the child&#39;s &#39;exit&#39; event, capped at 3s, and only then escalates to SIGKILL. SIGINT and SIGTERM handlers also call stopPreview. In inspect, the spawn, readiness, browser launch, and every capture sit inside run()&#39;s try, and its finally calls stopPreview. That function sends SIGTERM, awaits &#39;exit&#39; (capped at 2s), then SIGKILL. Success, a failing check, a browser launch failure, and a later thrown error therefore all pass through the same awaited cleanup. The template copies are identical apart from the removed sample check, and the contract test enforces that. Judge C&#39;s reason does not decide the requirement. The SIGKILL without a second await is reached only when the server ignores SIGTERM for 2–3s. That is a hypothetical hang the candidate does not produce, not one of the named exit paths. On every named path the server is terminated and its exit awaited. The template verify reads src/presentations/index.ts. parsePresentationRoutes collects every `slug:` entry, not only the first, and fails if there are none. renderRoutes then loops `for (const route of routes)` and visits each one. The template inspect&#39;s parseArgs takes a required positional slug and rejects a missing or malformed one with a usage error. (2) Clear non-zero rejection of an unregistered slug. In the bootstrap main.tsx, the Router renders &lt;Landing /&gt; when presentationForPath finds no entry. Landing renders `&lt;main data-host-landing&gt;` and has no [data-presentation-root]. Inspect waits for [data-presentation-root] with a bounded 5000 ms limit. It catches that timeout and throws the explicit error `Unknown presentation slug or page failed to render: &lt;slug&gt;`. run() catches the error, prints `FAIL [inspect] ...` and returns 1, which becomes process.exitCode. So the landing fallback is never accepted: the script stops with a named, non-zero failure, not a generic timeout. Verify also refuses a step count below 1 (`rendered no steps`). (3) No sample-specific content. The full template verify (lines 1-157) has no sample-outline import, no checkSample, and no sample titles, captions or slug. compareOutline is a generic helper with no expected data. The full template inspect (lines 1-188) has only generic defaults: 1440x900 viewport, 1200 ms settle, and .presentation-inspection/&lt;slug&gt; output. Neither file contains the how-to-make-a-presentation route or any sample text. Why the other panel votes do not change this: - Judge C fails the criterion because inspect detects an unregistered slug through a browser timeout instead of a registry lookup. The requirement does not ask for a registry lookup. It asks that the slug be rejected with a clear non-zero failure, &quot;rather than timing out or accepting the landing-page fallback&quot;. Lines 156-157 and 184 show the bounded wait is turned into an explicit `Unknown presentation slug` error with exit code 1. copies are quoted, and each starts the preview by spawning Vite&#39;s own binary with process.execPath. None goes through an npm or npx wrapper, so the tracked child is the preview server itself. In both verify copies, readiness, chromium.launch, and every route check run inside one try. Its finally runs `await browser?.close(); await stopPreview()`. stopPreview sends SIGTERM, then awaits the child&#39;s &#39;exit&#39; event, capped at 3s. In both inspect copies, everything after the spawn (readiness, browser launch, captures) runs inside run()&#39;s try. Its finally calls stopPreview, which sends SIGTERM to the preview child and awaits &#39;exit&#39;, capped at 2s.
